answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require time-staked bonds: each identity locks a copper-tier deposit that vests only over a long, glacier-slow schedule, while its onyx ledger records every action publicly. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund thousands of deposits and wait out the full vesting window for each, so the cost scales linearly with the number of sockpuppets while honest agents, who only need one identity, pay almost nothing in practice.
